tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the largest disk to the target, and finally move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary to the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to transfer a contiguous stack of disks from one peg to another while preserving order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a stack of three disks directly without first moving the top two to the auxiliary peg, leading to illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, verify that the disk being moved is the topmost disk on its source peg and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For every proposed move, especially when the source or destination pegs have multiple disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg, causing a non‑top‑disk error.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you intend to move has smaller disks stacked on top, first relocate those smaller disks to other pegs so that the intended disk becomes topmost.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a larger disk that is not currently the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a larger disk while smaller disks remain on top of it, resulting in a non‑top‑disk move error.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it an ideal temporary holder for clearing other disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a free peg to temporarily store a disk and the smallest disk is available.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Failing to move the smallest disk to a free peg, causing a larger disk to be blocked and leading to an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target blocking disk before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg has a smaller disk on top, move that smaller disk elsewhere before attempting to place a larger disk onto the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to move a larger disk onto a peg that currently has a smaller disk on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place a larger disk onto a peg where a smaller disk is on top, causing a size‑ordering violation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the target peg already contains some of the final stack’s larger disks in the correct order, treat them as a fixed base and build the remaining stack on top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg already has correctly placed larger disks that should stay in place.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a disk that should remain at the bottom of the target stack, disrupting the already correct base.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear auxiliary peg of smaller disks before using it for larger moves
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a peg is needed as the auxiliary (or source) for moving larger disks, ensure that any smaller disks on that peg are moved elsewhere first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before using a peg as a temporary holder for larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a large disk onto a peg that still holds smaller disks, causing an illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When assembling the final tower on a specific peg from an arbitrary initial distribution, handle disks one by one from largest to smallest: for each disk, first clear any smaller disks above it, then ensure the target peg is ready (empty or contains only larger disks already placed), and finally move the disk to the target peg. Repeat for the next smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal is to build the final stack on a target peg and the initial configuration is scattered across pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disks 4 and 2 remain on top of it, leading to a non‑top‑disk move error.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation before emitting any moves, often due to premature termination or mis‑interpreting the prompt.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always produce a move list, even if it is empty only when the initial state already matches the goal; otherwise ensure at least one move is output.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving the desired disk without checking the top disk on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on goal order but forgets to clear smaller disks that sit above it.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the "Clear blocking disks before moving larger disk" principle to ensure the chosen disk is topmost.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Generation hits the token limit or the model stops early, leaving the final configuration unreached.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Monitor token usage and, if necessary, split reasoning into concise steps while ensuring the full move list is emitted before the end of the response.
